stated: Work towards rejoining the EU as soon as politically feasible. Join the Customs Union as a first step, followed by a speedy return to free movement of people and rejoining the Erasmus Programme.

source.quote: Green MPs will work towards: • Re-joining the EU as soon as the domestic political situation is favourable and EU member states are willing. • Joining the Customs Union as a first step towards full EU membership, and a way of resolving many of the worst problems resulting from Brexit. • A speedy return to the free movement of people between the UK and the EU, including reciprocal rights to work for both UK and European citizens. • Rejoining the Erasmus Programme, which enables students to study for a year in another European country.

bearing_set.reason: Joining the Customs Union removes tariff and non-tariff friction on EU trade, directly affecting prices of food and goods in the household basket.
Restoring free movement of people materially reshapes UK labour markets — affecting wages, job competition, employment rights portability, and in-work mobility for ordinary workers.
Rejoining Erasmus is explicitly stated and directly affects educational access and opportunity for UK students and apprentices to study/train across Europe.

Full EU membership restores UK access to Europol, the European Arrest Warrant, and cross-border criminal intelligence databases — concrete mechanisms bearing on national security posture and crime/justice effectiveness.

EU membership would bind the UK to EU environmental law (Fit for 55, Water Framework Directive, Nature Restoration Law, EU ETS), directly affecting the UK's emissions trajectory and statutory air/water quality standards.

Full EU membership reinstates the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights as binding domestic law, strengthening the civil-rights and anti-discrimination legal framework — a concrete change to the legal-rights architecture.

Restoring free movement gives UK citizens the legal right to live, work and study across 27 EU countries — a direct expansion of personal liberty and freedom from state-imposed geographic restriction.
EU membership entails a net budget contribution (historically £10–15bn+ per year); this is a concrete, recurring fiscal cost that bears on public-finance sustainability.

Trade integration via Customs Union and single-market alignment materially affects UK productivity, business investment and real living standards — the dominant macroeconomic lever in most post-Brexit impact assessments.

Trade friction and tariffs bear disproportionately on lower-income households (higher food/goods share of spending); reversing them narrows the rich-poor gap in real purchasing power, moving the Gini-adjacent distributional indicator.

Large-scale resumption of free movement would substantially increase inward migration flows, generating non-negligible (if contested in direction) effects on social trust, integration and community cohesion indicators.

membership_note: This is a multi-component policy — Customs Union, free movement, Erasmus, eventual EU membership — each targeting a distinct mechanism; eight bearings reflect genuinely separate causal pathways, not padding.
